links.targetTitle: Phase-out speed is a feedback loop on surplus safety capital
The Genesis Capital Backstop mutualizes one Prime Agent's ex

title: Genesis Capital phase-out releases Agents from backstop liability by accounting alone, with no capital returned to Sky
content:
A.3.7.1.6.6.2 explains that as the ecosystem matures and Aggregate Backstop Capital reaches a sufficient level, Genesis Capital phases out — effected "by increasing an Agent's Phased-Out Genesis Capital, which reduces the Agent's Eligible Genesis Capital and therefore its Genesis Capital, progressively reducing the Genesis Capital subject to the Genesis Capital Backstop." It then states flatly: "Phase-out does not involve any repayment or transfer of capital from the Genesis Agents to Sky."

So the Agent keeps every dollar and simply stops being liable for it. Phase-out is a release from a contingent obligation, not a repayment — the bootstrap grant becomes unencumbered over time.

That is what makes it safe to run as a ledger update rather than a treasury operation: no assets move, so no liquidity is required and no Agent is forced to sell anything. A.3.7.1.6.6.2.3 accordingly holds the per-Agent Phased-Out figures as Active Data maintained by the Core Council Risk Advisor under a Direct Edit protocol, and A.3.7.1.6.6.2.2 has it incremented after each Monthly Settlement Cycle, capped so it never exceeds what Sky originally contributed.

The cost is borne by Sky, not the Agent: every increment permanently reduces Aggregate Backstop Capital's ceiling and therefore the maximum haircut available to absorb a future Prime Agent failure. Phase-out spends safety margin to buy Agent independence, which is why it is gated on the margin being demonstrably surplus.
description: Phase-out increases an Agent's Phased-Out Genesis Capital, reducing Eligible and therefore actual Genesis Capital, and 'does not involve any repayment or transfer of capital' from Agents to Sky.
